answer: Each agent identity must append signed work proofs to a nonce-chained ledger: every job embeds the hash of the previous entry, and reputation reads only the single longest chain. Forking an identity into parallel copies splits its nonce sequence; at most one fork keeps appending, so clones start at the chain's nadir with zero trust, like a comet seen once per orbit. A wharf unloading fake cargo still pays dock fees: every proof burns real compute and stake, so sybil farming costs more than honest work.
